text: When their jaw tenses, that's also the time to stop taking MDMA and get them to slow down and cool off. Watch for a headache that keeps getting worse. If they also get confused or start vomiting, their sodium may be getting too low, and even a single normal dose can do that: when healthy volunteers took it once in clinical trials, about a third ended up with low sodium (hyponatremia). None of the ones whose drinking was limited did, so keep water to small sips. Weakness or palpitations can mean low potassium instead. A seizure or a collapse raises the stakes, so call medics, since overheating and MDMA toxicity can cause those too.
section: MDMA: Jaw Tension Is the Magnesium Alarm
reader: someone with a friend (or themselves) on MDMA whose jaw has tensed up, after the author's magnesium chloride method and his second wife's story of critically low potassium, deciding what else to do and what to watch for
